title: Experiencing work through a placement or simulation
lesson_success_checks: Take part in the agreed work task through an accessible role. Keep a truthful progress record and handover. Reflect briefly on what went well and what was hard/unclear, self-assess five Week 1 expectations and choose a next step.
source_assessment_summary: Formative review; staff confirm any later accredited mapping from actual evidence.
accreditation: The qualification/accredited unit, mapping confirmed by staff; no named scheme or awarding body.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 3, 18–22 January 2027. Friday 22 January 2027, P1. One forty-minute formative lesson for a pair. Six-week term 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. Actual activity date/mode recorded separately; no clock time supplied.
timing: Recall expectations and safe reporting; confirm access and mode.
Model four stages, honest progress recording and handover.
Rehearse sequence, timed-list meaning and five expectations; private hinge.
Classroom shift: set up 2, make/check 4, record 3, hand over 3.
Short reflection, five self-ratings, private feedback/reply and save.

source_timing.note: Minute phases and twelve-minute shift authored for classroom simulation, not prescribed by row 90 or a real placement.

source_adaptation: B90 Spr1·W3 and C90 exact outcome retained. Inherited framework/resource context from row 88 generic. Row 90 gives no minute sequence: authored 5/8/10/12/5 lesson and twelve-minute classroom shift. Same business/order/roles as Week 1. Four task stages and timed list implement owner brief. School-arranged real placement replaces simulation and uses the neutral reflection sheet unchanged; actual placement tasks/timings arranged by school. Supported/Standard/Stretch retained.

sources.note: Uploaded snapshot read directly; B90/C90 exact. Inherited identifying labels generic. Raw workbook not distributed; no current repository check claimed.
Accepted business continuity, safety/help, editions/tier/cover structure and unchanged generic workroom image bank; only controlled view D is used in Week 3.
Business, order, roles, five expectation labels/meanings and four self-rating statements retained exactly. Reflection prompt for finished work is activity-neutral.

Friday 22 January P1, pair, forty minutes. Simulated shift with set up/make/record/hand over, timed job list, well/hard reflection and Week 1 expectations check. Real school-arranged placement replaces simulation; same reflection sheet unchanged. Weeks 4–6 one per return; pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Keep four numbered task cards, a short checklist, model and sentence starts. Read one step at a time; use usual aid, pointing, voice, typing or exact scribe. Adult can partner. Make your own brief log/reflection and five honest self-ratings.
routes.Standard: Use the task cards and timed list to agree roles, make/check, record actual progress and hand over. Give one example of what went well and what was hard or unclear. Rate all five expectations and choose a next step. Keep normal aids.
routes.Stretch: Compare the plan with actual progress and explain an adjustment that helped. Give a precise handover of unfinished checks and evaluate a limit of this short shift. Use the same individual reflection and five expectations; extra writing optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

task_cards.instruction: Read or hear the order. Check the two large cards and two strips, agreed space and roles. Ask if unsure.
task_cards.check: Preparer/checker roles agreed; written order and usual aid ready.

task_cards.instruction: Prepare two paper packs, each with one large card beside one strip. Check both against the order. Reset and swap roles for round two.
task_cards.check: Record what was actually prepared or checked; unfinished work stays visible.

task_cards.instruction: Keep your actual roles, task progress and any help or check still needed. Use counts only when you know them.
task_cards.check: Your own short log, with unknown or not tried where appropriate.

task_cards.instruction: Tell the next person what you did, what is ready and what still needs checking. Agree who takes the next step.
task_cards.check: A short accurate handover through your usual communication mode.

timed_jobs.job: Two short rounds, resetting and swapping roles.
Keep actual roles, progress and anything unfinished.
Say what is ready and what needs checking.

expectations.label: Readiness and reliability
expectations.meaning: Know the agreed start and task. Get agreed materials ready. Tell the supervisor if a delay or support need affects the plan.
expectations.look_for: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.

expectations.label: Respectful communication
expectations.meaning: Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
expectations.look_for: I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.

expectations.label: Instructions and quality
expectations.meaning: Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
expectations.look_for: I checked a step or the finished packs against the order.

expectations.label: Safety and help
expectations.meaning: Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
expectations.look_for: I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.

expectations.label: Teamwork and responsibility
expectations.meaning: Agree roles, share information and report mistakes honestly. Ask for a workable adjustment when needed.
expectations.look_for: I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

reflection_prompts: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.
I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.
I checked a step or finished work against the instruction.
I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.
I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.
rating_states: I did this with a prompt
placement_rule: A real placement arranged by the school replaces the classroom simulation. Use the same reflection sheet unchanged. School confirms tasks, supervision, access and actual timing separately; the twelve-minute classroom list is not a real-placement schedule. Record actual date, mode, task and evidence. If activity has not happened, mark pending and do not invent experience.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, business roles and progress/handover models are invented and declared. Actual task/date/mode/roles/progress/reflections recorded honestly. No real employer, person, product or place named.
private_help_route: Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal employment, family or accident account requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Neutral Evidence Sheet pages 2–3: blank work/reflection log and five-expectation review, used unchanged in both modes. Book/voice/aid/typing/exact scribe valid; read back/correct. Actual task/date/mode and unobserved parts retained.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: numbered cards, short checklist, one step and reduced quantity. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, written order, usual aid and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable routine, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear accessible table, seated roles and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: After the model ask whether both packs were checked. Key: only one. The other must be handed over as needing a check. Keep task/order/model in view; fade answer cues only. A normal reading/communication aid is access, not automatically a content prompt.

main_hinge.claim: Record partial progress and hand over the unfinished check honestly.

parallel_hinge.claim: Pause and ask about an unclear next step.

assessment: Keep actual task/role/progress and handover, a short what-went-well and hard/unclear reflection, five self-ratings, one actual example and next step/reply. Ratings exactly as Week 1: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Normal access distinct from supplied thinking. Missing role or opportunity is Not seen today. Judge reflection from evidence, not personality, pace or a real employment history.

evidence.description: Individual actual task/progress/handover log, short well/hard reflection, five self-ratings, evidence example and next step/reply.

where_this_leads: This helps me complete an agreed work routine, hand over accurately and use evidence to plan an improvement.
colour_blind_safe: Numbered stages, written time windows, labels and words carry meaning; no colour-only states.

asset.description: Unchanged generated workroom scene bank from accepted Week 2. Only controlled view D used, in native crops; generic invented workers/workplace.

sequence_next.scope: Not authored. One per return after Downloaded. Further GROW Careers paused.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Friday 22 January 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · LAUNCH · a pair of learners · Spring 1 Week 3 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term, 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. Thread tags: SMSC So/M (S/C none); British Values MR/IL (D/RL/T none).
Source: LAUNCH Weekly - Spring row 90, B90 Spr1·W3 and C90 exact. Inherited framework/resource context from row 88 generic; no registration or award completion inferred.

Take part in the agreed work task through an accessible role. Keep a truthful progress record and handover. Reflect briefly on what went well and what was hard/unclear, self-assess five Week 1 expectations and choose a next step.

An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
Keep the Week 1 two-pack order and supervisor/preparer/checker roles. Week 2 learning applies: keep the area clear, pause and report a concern. No real customer, money, data, employer or place.

Two large ready-cut cards and two strips per pair, plus spares; written order, task cards, timed list, tier packs, vocabulary, books or blank typed reflection and usual aids. Reset/reuse paper for round two; do not report reused materials as commercial output. Adult may take the partner role. Confirm private help and pause/return.

A real placement arranged by the school replaces the classroom simulation. Use the same reflection sheet unchanged. School confirms tasks, supervision, access and actual timing separately; the twelve-minute classroom list is not a real-placement schedule. Record actual date, mode, task and evidence. If activity has not happened, mark pending and do not invent experience.
This helps me complete an agreed work routine, hand over accurately and use evidence to plan an improvement.
Recall expectations and safe reporting; confirm access and mode.
Model four stages, honest progress recording and handover.
Rehearse sequence, timed-list meaning and five expectations; private hinge.
Classroom shift: set up 2, make/check 4, record 3, hand over 3.
Short reflection, five self-ratings, private feedback/reply and save.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes. Source row 90 gives no minute sequence; these phases are authored. Processing and brief pauses included. Simulation timings guide the routine, not speed or worth.

0–5: retrieve one Week 1 expectation and Week 2 keep-clear/report response. Confirm simulation or school-arranged placement mode. 5–9: explain set up, make/check, record and hand over. 9–13: model one checked pack and one still needing a check; record both honestly. Model handover: “One is ready; the other needs checking. Please check it before calling the order complete.” This is an invented example, not learner evidence.

13–19: order the four cards and rehearse a role agreement and handover with the written order visible. Read the relative shift clock: 0–2, 2–6, 6–9, 9–12. Preview the five self-rating labels; do not prefill judgements. 19–23: hinge B, report partial progress rather than call unfinished work complete. Parallel A, ask about an unclear next step rather than guess. Re-model and recheck privately.

23–25 set up: order, materials, access and roles. 25–29 make/check: two brief rounds with reset and swap, so each can try preparer and checker. 29–32 record: actual role and progress, known counts, unfinished checks, help and a brief evidence clue. 32–35 hand over: each learner gives a short update to adult/partner. Reduce repeats or quantity for access; record what happened, never manufacture completion. Keep a stable work area at the transition.

35–38: each gives one short what-went-well statement and one hard/not-tried/unclear statement, then rates the five expectations. Pointing or a scribed selection is valid. “Nothing was hard today” is valid; do not invent a difficulty. 38–40: privately check one evidence clue, set one NS and keep the reply/next check time; save individual record. Missing evidence stays visible.

Keep four numbered task cards, a short checklist, model and sentence starts. Read one step at a time; use usual aid, pointing, voice, typing or exact scribe. Adult can partner. Make your own brief log/reflection and five honest self-ratings.

Use the task cards and timed list to agree roles, make/check, record actual progress and hand over. Give one example of what went well and what was hard or unclear. Rate all five expectations and choose a next step. Keep normal aids.

Compare the plan with actual progress and explain an adjustment that helped. Give a precise handover of unfinished checks and evaluate a limit of this short shift. Use the same individual reflection and five expectations; extra writing optional.

After the model ask whether both packs were checked. Key: only one. The other must be handed over as needing a check. Keep task/order/model in view; fade answer cues only. A normal reading/communication aid is access, not automatically a content prompt.

The shift list is a twelve-minute classroom guide: 2 + 4 + 3 + 3. Pause or reduce repetitions when needed. If a task is unfinished, record and hand it over honestly. Do not race, remove a normal aid, or penalise a support need. An adult can partner; no forced peer performance. Role swap is planned, not fabricated if not attempted.

Cognition and Learning: numbered cards, short checklist, one step and reduced quantity. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, written order, usual aid and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable routine, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear accessible table, seated roles and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.

Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal employment, family or accident account requested.

Evidence Sheet pages 1–3 use neutral activity fields and the same five expectations. Use unchanged for simulation or school-arranged real placement; actual task/date can differ from the lesson. Page 2 blank typed work/reflection log; page 3 blank five-expectation review; page 4 staff record. Do not add an employer/place name. Book/usual aid default.

Keep actual task/role/progress and handover, a short what-went-well and hard/unclear reflection, five self-ratings, one actual example and next step/reply. Ratings exactly as Week 1: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Normal access distinct from supplied thinking. Missing role or opportunity is Not seen today. Judge reflection from evidence, not personality, pace or a real employment history.

VF, WS, I, NS, //, ?, E and R generic codes. E actual banked work. R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. One NS might add the unfinished check to a handover. Retain first try and response. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm any accredited mapping. A simulation does not prove real placement attendance or workplace competence.

Ready-cut paper only. No tools, machines, money, food, live customers, personal data or deliveries. Stop/keep clear/report if a real concern appears; follow actual school procedures. No staged hazard or cleanup activity. Real placement arrangements and approved tasks belong to the school; these cards do not replace induction or supervision.

Only Week 3 authored. W4 following instructions/teamwork, W5 customer service, W6 reflection/assessing follow one per return. Same invented business. Further GROW Careers paused. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures; keep concerns outside shared evidence.

I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Normal access aids do not automatically mean a content prompt.

Sequence: set up, make/check, record, hand over. Each pack has one large card beside one paper strip; two packs per round. Preparer arranges, checker compares both with the written order; reset and swap where possible. Record the actual role/count/check, not a claim all planned work happened.

Model has only one checked pack; other check unfinished. Handover must name that remaining check. Main B: record partial progress and hand it over honestly. Parallel A: pause and ask about an unclear next step. Re-model if needed, then recheck privately. Pass is unobserved.

Valid: “I prepared two packs in round one. I checked the next round with the order. One still needed checking at handover.” Only valid if observed/confirmed from actual work. Also valid: shorter partial record explaining what remains. Model numbers do not become learner evidence. Do not require full output to receive formative feedback.

Classroom windows 0–2, 2–6, 6–9, 9–12, durations 2/4/3/3. Total 12, lesson 23–35. Times guide routine; pause/reduce repeated work for access. A real placement uses school-arranged timing, not this shift clock.
What went well and what was hard

Accept a concrete work example, a support that helped, an unclear or not-tried step, or an honest “nothing hard today”. Avoid a forced personal account. Help turn “good” into one observable clue, such as checking against the order. A next step can be a small practice, clarification or more support.

Labels and four rating statements retained exactly from Week 1. A normal reading/communication aid is access; log content prompts separately. If self-rating differs from observation, ask privately for the clue and retain any revision. Not seen today is valid for an unattempted role or missing opportunity. No total score or personality judgement.
Individual actual task/progress/handover, short well/hard reflection, five ratings, one example and next step/reply. Do not count another learner’s work or adult model as independent evidence.

All reflection fields are activity-neutral; no paper-pack order or fixed shift duration is printed as a requirement on the reflection pages. Actual activity date/mode/task/role and evidence are recorded. Pending means unobserved; do not invent attendance, tasks or feelings.

Supported model/cards/frames; Standard actual routine and linked reflection; Stretch plan-versus-progress and adjustment. Every tier retains usual aids, exact scribe/readback, adult partner, private turn and plan in any language. Pass/pause/return. No public questioning or personal employment story.

Ready-cut paper only, no tools/equipment, money/data or real customers. Keep clear/report actual concerns and follow school procedures. Real placements have school-arranged approved tasks/supervision. E actual saved evidence; R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply in usual mode. Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.

Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.
